title: Exercise the remaining bot capabilities in a customer account
description:
**Phase 1 of 5.**

- **Blocked by:** `chatticus-2f2d87` (F-computer) — nothing below can run until a computer starts in the customer account
- **Unblocks:** an honest pitch page, and any claim about what a customer gets

---

## Why this exists

`chatticus-b88c0a` proved the **backbone substrate** end to end in a customer account: Google sign-in, organization record, cross-account role with ExternalId, enablement, AWS home, and a completed turn (`pong`).

That is a real milestone and it is also **one capability out of many**. `pong` is a **computerless** turn — capability `cpu`. Every capability that touches the computer is unexercised in a customer account.

This card owns the rest of the matrix so the gaps are visible up front rather than found one at a time by a customer.

## Coverage after `b88c0a`

| Capability | Customer account | Evidence / gap |
|---|---|---|
| Google sign-in | **Proven** | `dev.chattic.us` |
| Organization record + `tenant_id` | **Proven** | Invisible in UI — `chatticus-9c8dbf` |
| Cross-account role, ExternalId, AssumeRole | **Proven** | `CREATE_COMPLETE`, template unmodified |
| Org enablement + AWS home | **Proven** | Operator deviation — `chatticus-070cb4` |
| Bot creation | Kernel only | No UI — `chatticus-7622fd` |
| **Computerless turn (`cpu`)** | **Proven** | `pong` |
| Computer start (cross-account RunTask) | **Unproven** | `chatticus-2f2d87` |
| Terminal / shell actions | **Unproven** | Needs a computer first |
| Browser actions (Chromium) | **Unproven** | Needs a computer first |
| File actions (`/workspace`) | **Unproven, and predicted to fail** | See below |
| Approvals loop | **Unproven** | Consequential actions default to require-approval |
| Watch / takeover display | **Unproven** | |
| Spend ceiling enforcement | **Unproven** | The ceiling is what makes the price safe |
| Relocate / failover between hosts | **Unproven** | |

## One failure is predictable now, before running anything

**File actions will fail in a customer account as currently templated.**

`b88c0a` recorded that the published role CFN is scoped to `ChatticusComputers*` and **not** `ChatticusSnapshots`. `/workspace` depends on the S3 snapshot protocol for hydrate and publish — and per `chatticus-fbae4e` D3 (refuted 2026-09-07), that protocol is **permanent**, not a transitional artifact waiting for EFS. So a bot in a customer account cannot hydrate or publish `/workspace` without snapshot-bucket access the role does not grant.

That is a **template gap**, and by `chatticus-8a25af`'s rule a template change is **customer-visible** — an existing customer has to re-run it. Cheap now, expensive after the first customer.

Decide deliberately: does the snapshot bucket live in the Anthus account with the role granted cross-account access, or in the customer account created by the template? That choice changes both the template and where customer data rests — which is the pitch page's central claim.

## Sequence

1. `chatticus-2f2d87` **F-computer** — a computer starts at all. Everything else is blocked on it.
2. **Terminal**, then **browser** — the two computer capabilities with no storage dependency.
3. **File actions** — expect the snapshot-bucket failure above; resolve the template question.
4. **Approvals** — a consequential action pauses and resumes correctly across the account boundary.
5. **Spend ceiling** — enforcement is what makes the floated price safe.
6. **Relocate / failover** — last; the least likely to be exercised by an early customer.

Stop and record at the first failure in each row rather than pushing through. A labeled stop is a result.

## Record

Same discipline as `b88c0a`: wiki runbook with placeholders, real ids in gitignored `AGENTS.local.md`, every deviation labeled. Add elapsed time per capability — the ~19 min provisioning figure covers **none** of this.

## Done when

Each row above is proven, or has a recorded failure with a decision about what changes — template, infrastructure, or product scope.
